title: Optimizing PyTorch Inference with LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems

mechanism.domainTask: LLM multi-agent optimization of PyTorch inference implementations for GPU performance
mechanism.populationDetail: PIKE-B uses a flat branching seed population with short-term solution history and no islands; default PIKE-O uses three islands with separate solution histories.
mechanism.archiveDetail: Default PIKE-O maintains an archive of 12 elite solutions; PIKE-B uses top-k history to seed new rounds but has no separately specified archive.
mechanism.replacementDetail: PIKE-B rebuilds its next seed batch by replicating the top-k valid solutions while retaining valid solution history. PIKE-O's archive/population update is inherited from OpenEvolve and its exact survivor replacement rule is not fully detailed.
mechanism.generationDetail: PIKE-B and PIKE-O mutation variants condition a broad rewrite on one selected implementation; default PIKE-O uses crossover prompts with five or more elite solutions as inspirations.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Validity/correctness status, runtime/speedup, and compilation or tolerance errors are used for filtering, ranking, and EFA repair.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Selection varies by strategy: PIKE-B has one seed per prompt from top-k; PIKE-O mutation uses one seed, while crossover uses multiple elite inspirations. Exact number across all variants is not singular.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: A modular multi-agent workflow separates idea brainstorming, code optimization, evaluation, and error repair; EFA is an iterative diagnostic-conditioned repair loop tightly integrated with correctness/performance evaluation.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/Optimizing PyTorch Inference with LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: The paper is cited in the application section's KernelBench usage table, but its PIKE population, archive, prompt, generation, evaluation, and explore/exploit mechanisms are not currently covered in mechanism taxonomy prose. Distinguish PIKE-B from PIKE-O; several placements apply only to a named configuration. The PIKE-O archive replacement rule is inherited/underspecified.
